title: See the wood chipper at the Fargo visitor centre
description: The actual prop from the film, kept behind glass with a hat you can borrow for the photograph. Free, and the town leans into it.

title: Walk On-A-Slant Indian Village at Fort Lincoln
description: Reconstructed Mandan earth lodges on a village site occupied for two centuries, beside the fort Custer rode out from in 1876.

title: Cross into the International Peace Garden
description: A garden straddling the border since 1932, where you can walk between two countries. Bring a passport to leave from either side.

title: Drive the Enchanted Highway sculptures
description: Thirty-two miles of county road with the world's largest scrap-metal sculptures beside it, built by one man to keep his town alive.

title: Ice fish on Devils Lake
description: A lake with no outlet that has quadrupled in size since 1993, drowning farms. In winter the ice roads carry trucks and fish houses.

title: See the Dells sandstone from the water
description: Narrow sandstone gorges cut by a glacial flood, photographed by H H Bennett in the 1800s, which is why the tourism happened at all.

title: See the Calatrava wings open at the Milwaukee Art Museum
description: A 27-metre brise soleil that opens at ten, closes at five and flaps once at noon, over a gallery on the lakefront.

title: See the Circus World collection at Baraboo
description: The Ringling Brothers wintered here from 1884, and the largest collection of circus wagons in the world is in the original buildings.

title: Climb the East Bluff at Devil's Lake
description: Quartzite bluffs 150 metres above a lake with no inlet or outlet, dammed at both ends by glacial moraine.

title: Take the Lambeau Field tour
description: The oldest continually operating NFL stadium, in a town of 105,000 that owns its own club through shareholders who get no dividend.

title: Ride the Cass Scenic Railroad up Bald Knob
description: Shay geared locomotives built for logging, climbing an eleven per cent grade to the third highest point in the state.

title: Walk to Jefferson Rock at Harpers Ferry
description: Where two rivers and three states meet, and where John Brown's raid in 1859 helped bring on the war. The lower town is kept as it was.

title: Look up at Seneca Rocks
description: A quartzite fin standing 275 metres above the valley, the only true summit in the east that requires technical climbing to reach.

title: See Blackwater Falls in the Canaan Valley
description: Amber water from hemlock tannin over a 17-metre drop, in a high valley that holds snow when the rest of the state has none.

title: Go down the Beckley Exhibition Coal Mine
description: A retired miner drives you 450 metres into a seam and explains the work. It is the honest counterweight to the scenery above ground.

title: Tour the Ben and Jerry's factory
description: Thirty minutes, a sample at the end, and a flavour graveyard outside with headstones for the discontinued.

title: Walk Mount Tom above Woodstock
description: The only national park telling the story of conservation forestry, on a hillside replanted in the 1870s after Vermont was logged bare.

title: See the steamboat inside the Shelburne Museum
description: Thirty-nine buildings moved onto one site, including a 67-metre Lake Champlain steamboat hauled overland in 1955.

title: Drive the Northeast Kingdom in October
description: The emptiest corner of the state, named by a senator in 1949, where the colour peaks a week before the rest of New England.

title: Ski Killington into May
description: The longest season in the east, usually opening in October and closing after the rest have melted, on six mountains.

title: Walk Lincoln's Springfield
description: The only house he ever owned, on a block kept as it was in the 1860s. Free, with timed tickets from the visitor centre.

title: Walk the Garden of the Gods in Shawnee forest
description: Sandstone weathered into stacked slabs above the forest canopy in the far south, closer to Kentucky than Chicago and nothing like either.

title: Walk the canyons at Starved Rock
description: Eighteen sandstone canyons cut by glacial meltwater, with waterfalls after rain and frozen falls in a hard January.

title: Climb Monks Mound at Cahokia
description: The largest earthwork in the Americas, at the centre of a city of perhaps twenty thousand people in 1100 AD, larger than London then.

title: See how a Louisville Slugger is turned
description: Bats made on the same site since 1884, still turned to order for players, with a 36-metre steel bat leaning on the building.

title: See the moonbow at Cumberland Falls
description: One of very few places in the world with a predictable lunar rainbow, visible on clear nights around the full moon.

title: Watch the elk and bison at Land Between the Lakes
description: A restored prairie herd on a peninsula between two reservoirs, with a driving loop and a dark sky observatory nearby.

title: Drive the horse farms around Lexington
description: Limestone under the pasture puts calcium in the grass, which is the reason the thoroughbred industry settled exactly here.

title: Walk into Providence Canyon
description: Gullies up to 45 metres deep cut entirely by bad farming practice in the 1800s. A man-made accident that became the state's canyon.

title: Walk to Amicalola Falls
description: The tallest cascade in the south-east at 222 metres, with 604 steps beside it and the Appalachian Trail approach starting at the top.

title: See a band in Athens
description: R.E.M. and the B-52s came out of the same few blocks, and the 40 Watt Club still books new bands most nights of the week.

title: Walk Driftwood Beach on Jekyll Island
description: A boneyard beach of bleached oaks killed by erosion, best at low tide, on an island the state bought in 1947 to keep public.

title: Drive the Blue Ridge Parkway from Roanoke
description: Three peaks over a lake at milepost 86, with a walk up Sharp Top on a shuttle bus if you would rather not climb it.

title: See the stalacpipe organ at Luray Caverns
description: Rubber mallets strike stalactites across 14,000 square metres to play music, which makes it the largest instrument on earth.

title: Walk False Cape by foot or bike only
description: Reachable only on foot, by bike or by boat, which is why nine kilometres of Atlantic beach here stay empty in July.

title: Walk Monticello and the enslaved quarters
description: Jefferson's house and, since 2018, the restored Mulberry Row where the people he enslaved lived and worked. Both are the tour now.

title: Cycle Nantucket to Sconset
description: Cobbled streets, a whaling museum, and a flat bike path to a village of rose-covered cottages at the far end.

title: Walk Salem outside October
description: The witch trial memorial is a quiet stone bench court. In October the town is unusable; any other month it is a serious maritime port.

title: Walk around Walden Pond
description: A kettle pond with a marked cabin site and a swimming beach. Parking is capped, so arrive early on a summer weekend.

title: Ride a swan boat in the Public Garden
description: Pedal-powered by one person hidden in the swan since 1877, run by the same family the whole time.

title: Drive the North Cascades Highway
description: Closed by avalanche risk from November to spring. Diablo Lake is turquoise from glacial flour ground off the rock above it.

title: Walk the Enchantments day route
description: Thirty-two kilometres point to point over Aasgard Pass, or an overnight if you win the permit lottery. Mountain goats will follow you.

title: Walk the Georgia O'Keeffe landscape at Ghost Ranch
description: The cliffs she painted for forty years, with a dinosaur quarry on the same property that produced thousands of Coelophysis skeletons.

title: Walk into the Gila Cliff Dwellings
description: Forty rooms built into five caves by Mogollon people in the 1280s and abandoned within a generation. You walk right into them.

title: See a show at Red Rocks
description: Two 90-metre sandstone monoliths forming natural acoustics. Free to walk and use for exercise on any day without a show.

title: Ride the Durango and Silverton narrow gauge
description: Coal-fired steam on 914mm gauge along a ledge above the Animas gorge, running the same route since 1882.

title: Drive the Historic Columbia River Highway
description: The first scenic highway in the country, built 1913 to a grade gentle enough for early cars, past a string of waterfalls.

title: See the bluebonnets in the Hill Country
description: Lady Bird Johnson's roadside planting programme is why the verges go blue for three weeks each spring. Free, and everyone stops.

title: See the riverbanks and the Congaree at Columbia
description: Twenty kilometres of free riverside path where three rivers meet, with the old canal locks still in place along it.

title: Raft the US National Whitewater Center
description: The largest man-made whitewater river in the world, pumped in a loop, and an Olympic training site open to anyone who turns up.

title: Climb an Adirondack High Peak
description: Forty-six summits over 4,000 feet, and a club for anyone who does all of them. Cascade is the usual first one.

title: Drive the farm roads of Little Compton
description: Stone walls, a colonial common and no through traffic, in the corner of the state most Rhode Islanders keep to themselves.
